dimension: Harmony identity and total patch surface, and collision with TAOM's patches
summary: BannerlordCoop registers FOUR Harmony owner ids — "Bannerlord.Coop" (the main one, carrying all explicit patches plus the entire AutoSync transpiler engine), "Coop.UILoading", "Coop.BootFix", and "CoopAutoRegistryFactory" — none of which TAOM's PatchShield allowlist protects, and its module id "Coop" is not in TAOM's CoopPresence detection list. It never unpatches other owners and never asserts exclusivity; the only Unpatch call targets its own patch-method handles. It ships 0Harmony 2.4.2.0, byte-identical in version+commit hash to TAOM's vendored copy, so one Harmony assembly is loaded process-wide and both mods' instances see each other's patches — the mechanical prerequisite for coexistence is satisfied. The patch surface is enormous (653 files carrying [HarmonyPatch], 620 prefixes / 232 postfixes / 31 finalizers / 42 explicit transpiler files, plus 195 generated transpilers applied to EVERY declared method and constructor of 41 campaign types), and it intersects TAOM on 39 types and 17 exact methods. Two hard-conflict classes exist: a genuine transpiler-on-transpiler collision on HeroCreator.DeliverOffSpring, and three prefix-returns-false replacements that will silently disable TAOM features (PartyBaseHelper.HasFeat is the worst — both mods install a mutually-exclusive skip-original prefix). Separately, FragileDetourGuard patches HarmonyLib's own PatchTools.DetourMethod and can suppress ANY mod's transpiler-only detour applied after Coop's PatchAll, which includes TAOM's entire OnGameInitializationFinished batch in a hosted session.

findings.claim: BannerlordCoop's PRIMARY Harmony owner id is the exact literal "Bannerlord.Coop". This single instance owns every explicit patch in GameInterface, every Missions patch category, and the whole AutoSync transpiler engine. TAOM's PatchShield protected-owner allowlist does not contain it, so PatchShield's rescue path is free to strip it.

findings.claim: TRANSPILER-ON-TRANSPILER COLLISION on HeroCreator.DeliverOffSpring. Coop's HeroFieldPatches yields it from TargetMethods and applies ELEVEN separate stfld-rewriting transpilers to it; TAOM's Patch13_RaceAge applies its own transpiler to the same method. This is the only true transpiler-vs-transpiler case between the two mods.

TAOM already has a LogTranspilerDegradation path (line 110); verify it fires rather than throwing when the pattern is absent, and confirm the degradation is logged, not silent.

findings.claim: PREFIX-VS-PREFIX MUTUAL EXCLUSION on PartyBaseHelper.HasFeat. Coop installs a prefix that unconditionally sets __result and returns false (skipping the original AND every later prefix). TAOM's Patch18_CulturalFeats installs a prefix with the identical shape. Harmony skips remaining prefixes once one returns false, so exactly one of the two implementations wins and the other is silently dead — whichever loses, a feature breaks with no exception and no log.
findings.taom_impact: Convert Main/Features/CulturalFeats/Hooks/PartyBaseHelper_HasFeat_Patch.cs from a skip-original Prefix to a Postfix that adjusts __result, OR gate the whole Patch18_CulturalFeats category off when CoopPresence.IsActive. findings.claim: PREFIX-VS-POSTFIX ORDERING HAZARD on CaravansCampaignBehavior.CanTradeWith. Coop's prefix fully replaces the method (returns false) and resolves __result from its own session service. findings.claim: FragileDetourGuard patches HarmonyLib's OWN internal PatchTools.DetourMethod with a prefix that can return false, cancelling the detour. This is a process-global effect on every mod's patching, not just Coop's. A method that is 'fragile' (x64 unwind data within 5 bytes of function start), performs no stfld, and has no existing prefix/postfix/finalizer will have its detour SKIPPED — which is precisely the profile of a transpiler-only patch on a small method.

The cheapest mitigation is to pair each transpiler-only patch with a trivial no-op Prefix, which makes HasLoadBearingPatch return true and forces the detour through.

dimension: Policy / authority model, and whether the CLIENT ticks the campaign
summary: The client DOES tick the campaign. BannerlordCoop does not suppress the client's campaign loop: `Campaign.Tick` carries only a Postfix, `CampaignEventDispatcher.HourlyTick` runs on the client, `GameStateManagerPatches` actively FORCES `MapState.OnTick` to run even when MapState is not the active game state, and the client's `MapTimeTracker._numTicks` advances locally under a rate-slewing correction toward the server clock (250 ms `CampaignTimePacket` heartbeats). Only `Campaign.PartiesThink` is client-blocked. The mod's entire anti-double-run strategy is a hand-curated allowlist of 129 `RegisterEvents` prefixes over VANILLA behavior types only — 42 gated `return ModInformation.IsServer` (client-suppressed), 80 `return false` (dead on both peers). Nothing generic exists: every third-party CampaignBehavior, including all ~10 TAOM tick behaviors, registers and fires DailyTick/HourlyTick on BOTH peers. An unauthorized client write to a synced field is neither blocked nor thrown — it logs `Logger.Error("Client updated managed …")` and applies locally without broadcasting, so divergence is silent. TAOM CAN be made compatible: `Common.ModInformation.IsServer` is a public static authority flag and `GameInterface.Policies.CallOriginalPolicy.IsOriginalAllowed()` is a public gate, but `IsServer` defaults to `false` (so `IsClient` is TRUE in single-player) and must be ANDed with an active-session check via `ContainerProvider.TryGetContainer`.

findings.claim: The client ticks the campaign. Campaign.Tick is patched with a Postfix only — there is no prefix anywhere in the tree that suppresses it on the client.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM cannot rely on the client being frozen. Every TAOM CampaignBehavior tick handler runs on both peers unless TAOM gates it itself.

findings.claim: BannerlordCoop suppresses double-ticking ONLY via a hand-written per-vanilla-type allowlist of RegisterEvents prefixes. There is no generic CampaignBehaviorBase.RegisterEvents patch — grep for `HarmonyPatch(typeof(CampaignBehaviorBase` returns nothing, and the 42 client-suppressed types are all vanilla (MilitiasCampaignBehavior, VillageGoodProductionCampaignBehavior, TownSecurityCampaignBehavior, …).
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must author its own equivalent gate. The cheapest faithful copy of coop's own idiom is a single early-return in each TAOM behavior's RegisterEvents (or one TAOM-owned Harmony prefix over TAOM's own behavior types) returning false when a coop client session is active. TAOM behaviors needing gating: AlignmentDesertionBehavior, CareerQuestCampaignBehavior, CastleRecruitmentBehavior, CultureConversionBehavior, CultureMarketplaceBehavior, WarOfTheRingBehavior, MessengerCampaignBehavior, RaceAgeBehavior, SiegeDefenseBehavior, WarOfTheRingMomentumBehavior.

findings.claim: The client's campaign clock advances locally and is slewed toward the server, not driven by the server. Campaign.TickMapTime runs its vanilla original on the client; the coop postfix only applies a correction delta to MapTimeTracker._numTicks.
findings.taom_impact: Campaign day/hour boundaries are crossed independently on the client. Any TAOM DailyTick that mutates shared state will fire on the client at (approximately) the same campaign day the server fires it — a genuine double-run, not a near-miss.

findings.claim: The client's map state is force-ticked even when the player is in a non-map game state, and the vanilla ability to pause the active state is disabled.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM features that assume the campaign is paused while a menu/inventory/mission screen is open (encounter menus, settlement inventory writes, tournament flow) lose that assumption on the client. Any TAOM code relying on `Campaign.Current.TimeControlMode == Stop` as a mutual-exclusion device is invalid under coop.

findings.claim: An unauthorized client write to a synced field is NOT blocked and does NOT throw. It logs an Error and still applies the value locally, without publishing it to the network — silent divergence plus log spam.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM will not crash under coop — it will quietly desync. There is no exception to catch and no engine-level backstop. TAOM cannot detect its own divergence at runtime; the only signal is `Client updated managed …` Error lines in Coop_client.log. Any TAOM QA pass must grep that log, because gameplay looks superficially fine.

findings.claim: `ModInformation.IsServer` defaults to false, so `ModInformation.IsClient` evaluates TRUE in ordinary single-player whenever the Coop module is merely installed. It is only set at session start.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must NEVER gate on `IsClient` alone — doing so would disable every TAOM tick behavior in single-player for anyone subscribed to Coop. The correct predicate is `coopSessionActive && ModInformation.IsClient`, where session-active comes from `ContainerProvider.TryGetContainer(out _)`.

findings.claim: `ContainerProvider.Alive` is broken — it is a static readonly auto-property initialized once at type-init, when `_lifetimeScope` is still null, so it is permanently false. `TryGetContainer` is the working session-active probe.
findings.taom_impact: If TAOM binds to `ContainerProvider.Alive` for its coop-detection, every gate silently disables itself and TAOM double-runs. Bind to `TryGetContainer` instead (or reflect the private `_lifetimeScope`).

findings.claim: `ModInformation.IsServer` has a public setter with no guard. Any mod in the load order can flip the coop mod's entire authority model.
findings.evidence_quote: public static bool IsServer { get; set; } = false;
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must read this property and never write it. Worth an explicit comment at the TAOM call site — an accidental assignment would corrupt every coop session, not just TAOM's features.

findings.claim: Authority is a single global process-wide boolean, not per-object. There is no per-entity ownership model for world state; per-entity control exists only for player-controlled Heroes/Clans via PlayerManager.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM's design decision is binary and simple: world-mutating behaviors run server-only; there is no 'this client owns these settlements' middle ground to exploit. Player-facing TAOM features (career screen, own-party inventory) may still run on the client if scoped to `hero.IsControlledByThisInstance()`.

findings.claim: The client CAN legitimately mutate synced state by entering an AllowedThread scope — a [ThreadStatic] counter that makes CallOriginalPolicy return true. This is the escape hatch coop's own network handlers use to apply server-sent state.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must NOT use this to force through its own client-side writes — it suppresses the divergence warning without making the write authoritative (the value is applied locally and still never broadcast). Only useful if TAOM ever builds its own server→client message and applies it on the client. Note it is thread-local: TAOM code running off the game thread would not inherit the scope.

findings.claim: 80 vanilla CampaignBehaviors are disabled on BOTH peers (unconditional `return false` on RegisterEvents) — including CampaignWarManagerBehavior, IssuesCampaignBehavior, PregnancyCampaignBehavior, AgingCampaignBehavior, MarriageOfferCampaignBehavior, LordDefectionCampaignBehavior, PrisonerRecruitCampaignBehavior, NPCEquipmentsCampaignBehavior.
findings.taom_impact: Separate from the double-tick problem: TAOM features that observe or extend these vanilla behaviors get no events under coop on EITHER peer. TAOM's Diplomacy/WarOfTheRing work sits directly on top of the disabled CampaignWarManagerBehavior, and RaceAgeBehavior sits alongside the disabled AgingCampaignBehavior. Needs a separate per-feature audit.

findings.claim: All coop patches are applied uncategorized to both roles — there is no client build vs server build of the patch set. Role differentiation happens entirely inside patch bodies via ModInformation. `UnpatchAll()` is an empty method, so patches survive session teardown for the process lifetime.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM's gate must be evaluated live at each tick, not cached at load. After a player leaves a coop session, `ContainerProvider.Clear()` runs (making TryGetContainer false) but `ModInformation.IsServer` retains its last value and coop's patches stay installed — a stale cached 'am I a client' would permanently disable TAOM's behaviors for the rest of the process.

findings.claim: Campaign.TimeControlMode's setter is unconditionally blocked (two separate prefixes, both returning false) and its getter is overridden from a static mirror. Time changes are proposals routed client→server→broadcast.
findings.taom_impact: Any TAOM code that assigns `Campaign.Current.TimeControlMode` (e.g. to pause for a cutscene, menu, or event) becomes a no-op under coop on BOTH peers. TAOM must audit its assignments to that property and either drop them under coop or route through `ITimeControlInterface.AddUnpausePolicy` (public, WeakDelegate-based).

integration_api.how_taom_uses_it: The single canonical 'may I mutate shared state right now' gate, and the exact predicate coop's own AutoSync interceptors use. `IsOriginalAllowed()` returns true when (a) the calling thread is inside an AllowedThread scope, or (b) no ISyncPolicy is registered (no session), or (c) the session's policy says the current state is non-syncing. dimension: Module entry point, lifecycle, and load-order requirements
summary: TAOM and Coop can coexist in one AppDomain, but only after TAOM changes four things it currently gets wrong. Coop's entry point is `Coop.CoopMod : NoHarmonyLoader : MBSubModuleBase`; it applies three Harmony patches in its *constructor* (before any `OnSubModuleLoad` runs), installs its own version-blind `AssemblyResolve` in `NoHarmonyInit()` (called from `OnSubModuleLoad`), registers two `InitialStateOption`s in `NoHarmonyLoad()`, and defers its main patch batch + Roslyn AutoSync compile until a co-op session actually starts — on a background thread. It ships 0Harmony at exactly 2.4.2.0/PublicKeyToken=null, the same identity TAOM ships, so a single shared patch registry is achievable and is what TAOM's existing redirect already produces when TAOM loads first. The real hazards are: (1) TAOM's `RedirectBundledDependencies` matches on simple name and *ignores the requested version*, and TAOM+Coop both claim six overlapping names whose versions differ (Serilog 2.0.0.0 vs 4.2.0.0, `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe` 4.0.4.1 vs 6.0.1.0), so TAOM can hand Coop's Serilog-4.x-compiled code a Serilog 2 — including inside Roslyn's `Assembly.Load` at AutoSync build time; (2) TAOM's co-op interop plumbing (`ModulesToLoadAfterThis`, `coop-modules.txt`, `CoopPresence`) does not know the id `Coop` at all, so none of TAOM's co-op guards would engage; (3) Coop's `ModuleValidator` demands exact module-id + version equality across host and client for every non-official module, and rejects any OfficialOptional (DLC) module outright; (4) `FragileDetourGuard` prefixes `HarmonyLib.PatchTools.DetourMethod` process-globally and skips detours on methods with no prefix/postfix/finalizer, which is exactly the shape of TAOM's seven transpiler-only patches. Coop does not use UIExtenderEx, ButterLib or MCM anywhere in the decompiled tree, so there is no mixin collision on shared screens.

findings.claim: Coop applies Harmony patches in the SubModule CONSTRUCTOR, which the engine runs for every module before any OnSubModuleLoad. TAOM cannot pre-empt these three patches with anything registered in OnSubModuleLoad — only with TAOM.Dependencies' type static cctor, which fires at TAOM.Dependencies' own construction.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must accept that Coop's BootPatches (FontFactory.DefaultFont getter prefix, Font.TryLoadFontFromPath postfix, GauntletLayer.LoadMovieAux prefix) are already live before TAOM.SubModule.OnSubModuleLoad, and before TAOM.Dependencies installs PatchShield and the UnpatchAll guard. PatchShield's protected-owner allowlist must therefore include 'Coop.BootFix' from the compiled defaults or coop-modules.txt, not rely on being installed first. Also note CoopMod's ctor sets MBDebug.DisableLogging = false globally for every session, co-op or not.

findings.claim: The engine constructs ALL SubModule instances in module-list order first, then calls OnSubModuleLoad on all of them in that same order. Load-order pinning therefore controls both passes.

findings.taom_impact: Confirms TAOM's premise: pinning TAOM.Dependencies before Coop in the launcher order means TAOM.Dependencies' SubModule static cctor (which calls InstallAssemblyResolveHandler) runs before CoopMod's constructor. AddSubModule invokes the ctor at line 149 ('MBSubModuleBase value = (MBSubModuleBase)constructor.Invoke(new object[0]);') and InitializeSubModuleBases() is not called until line 1102, after the whole per-module loop completes. TAOM must add '<Module Id="Coop" />' to Dependencies/_Module/SubModule.xml's ModulesToLoadAfterThis to secure this.

findings.claim: Coop installs an AssemblyResolve handler that claims 13 assembly simple names, six of which overlap TAOM's own version-blind redirect list — and TAOM ships DIFFERENT versions of all six.
findings.taom_impact: Verified identities on disk: Coop ships Serilog 4.2.0.0, System.Memory 4.0.2.0, System.Buffers 4.0.4.0, System.Numerics.Vectors 4.1.5.0, System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe 6.0.1.0, System.Collections.Immutable 9.0.0.2. TAOM ships Serilog 2.0.0.0, System.Memory 4.0.1.1, System.Buffers 4.0.3.0, System.Numerics.Vectors 4.1.4.0, System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe 4.0.4.1, System.Collections.Immutable 1.2.5.0. TAOM's handler is registered first (pre-Native module) and .NET invokes AssemblyResolve subscribers in registration order until one returns non-null, so TAOM's handler answers first for every one of these names. Coop's Common.dll/GameInterface.dll are compiled against the 4.x/6.x/9.x APIs. TAOM MUST make RedirectBundledDependencies version-aware.

findings.claim: TAOM's AssemblyResolve handler matches on simple name only and returns the first loaded assembly with that name, discarding the requested version entirely.
findings.taom_impact: 'requested.Version' is parsed and never read. Fix: after a name match, compare loaded.GetName().Version to requested.Version and return null when the loaded version is lower, so the CLR falls through to Coop's handler or Coop's own bin. The comment at SubModule.cs:33-37 states the intent is to shadow other mods' bundled copies with TAOM's — that intent is wrong here because TAOM's copies are OLDER. Minimum viable alternative: drop 'Serilog', 'System.Memory', 'System.Buffers', 'System.Numerics.Vectors', 'System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe', 'System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions' from RedirectedSimpleNames when a co-op module is active.

findings.claim: Coop's AutoSync Roslyn compile calls Assembly.Load with both partial and full names, so the version-blind TAOM handler can poison the metadata references the generated sync assembly is compiled against.
findings.taom_impact: These Load calls run in the default Load context, which does not probe Coop's module bin, so AssemblyResolve fires and TAOM's handler answers first. Assembly.Load("System.Numerics.Vectors") is a bare partial name — TAOM returns 4.1.4.0 where Coop expects 4.1.5.0. The full-name loop covers GameInterface.dll's references, which include Serilog 4.2.0.0. If either resolves to TAOM's copy, cSharpCompilation.Emit either fails outright (throwing InvalidOperationException at line 116) or emits an assembly bound to the wrong Serilog. Same fix as the finding above; listed separately because it fires on a code path (Roslyn compile at co-op session start) that no main-menu smoke test will exercise.

findings.claim: Coop's main Harmony batch and the Roslyn AutoSync compile are deferred to co-op session start and run on a BACKGROUND thread, not the game thread.

dimension: Extension points for third-party mods — can TAOM register its own synced state through BannerlordCoop without modifying Coop's assemblies?
summary: There is NO documented, intentional third-party extension API in BannerlordCoop — grep for "plugin", "extension point", "third party", "public api", "IExtension", "RegisterExternal" returns zero hits across all 3266 decompiled files. However, three undocumented but load-bearing mechanisms make TAOM state-sync achievable without touching Coop's DLLs: (1) the Autofac composition root registers handlers by scanning the ENTIRE AppDomain filtered on namespace PREFIX (`InterfaceCollector.GetInterfaces<IHandler>("GameInterface")`, `RegisterAllTypesWithInterface<ClientModule, IHandler>` → `typeof(ClientModule).Namespace` = "Coop.Core.Client"), so a TAOM class declared in a namespace starting `GameInterface.`, `Coop.Core.Client.` or `Coop.Core.Server.` and implementing `Common.Messaging.IHandler` is auto-registered, constructor-injected with `IMessageBroker`/`INetwork`/`IObjectManager`, and AutoActivated; (2) `SerializableTypeMapper.CollectProtoContracts()` scans every non-dynamic AppDomain assembly for `[ProtoContract]` and derives wire ids as an FNV-1a hash of `Type.FullName`, so TAOM's own message types serialize with zero Coop changes; (3) the send/receive path is completely type-agnostic — `CoopNetworkBase.SendAll(IMessage)` and `CoopServer.OnNetworkReceive` accept any `IMessage` with no allowlist. Separately, `GameInterface.ContainerProvider` is a public static service locator (`TryResolve<T>`) giving TAOM read access to every container service from anywhere. The AutoSync codegen path, by contrast, is BLOCKED for TAOM-declared types: `AutoSyncModule.GetAutoSyncClasses()` scans only `GetType().Assembly` (GameInterface), and `AutoSyncBuilder.Build()` builds its Roslyn metadata-reference list from GameInterface + BCL + GameInterface's referenced assemblies only — TAOM.dll is never referenced, so generated `using TAOM.Features…;` would not compile. TAOM must therefore hand-write its handler/message pairs rather than register fields with AutoSync. One large free win: the join baseline is a full vanilla `Game.Current.Save(...)` into an in-memory driver (`SaveInterface.SaveCurrentGame`), so TAOM's SaveableTypeDefiner-persisted state (WotR momentum, culture-conversion holds, special resources) already reaches joining clients — only ongoing deltas need wire sync.

findings.claim: AutoSyncRegistry itself IS public and container-resolvable, and its AddField/AddProperty/AddSerializer/AddTargetMethod methods are public — so runtime registration is mechanically possible even though the codegen then fails for TAOM-owned types.
findings.taom_impact: Useful only if TAOM wants to sync a field on a TaleWorlds type that Coop does not already cover (that IS possible — TaleWorlds assemblies are referenced). findings.claim: There is NO awareness of specific other mods, no whitelist, and no compatibility shim for any named mod. Module handling is purely a generic client/server list-equality check.

dimension: Save/load model, save-definer collision, and version/mod-list validation
summary: There is NO save-definer collision: BannerlordCoop ships exactly two SaveableTypeDefiners, at base ids 44177000 and 44182000, roughly 682 million apart from TAOM's 726900501/601/701/801 — so the hard `Dictionary.Add` duplicate-key crash in `DefinitionContext` cannot fire from this pairing. The save transfer is the host's real, full engine .sav produced by `Game.Current.Save(...)` into an in-memory driver, Deflate-compressed (not LZ4 — LZ4 is only used for mission movement packets), chunked at 64 KiB, and loaded on the client through `SaveManager.Load("", driver, loadAsLateInitialize: true)` — bit-for-bit the same call vanilla's `MBSaveLoad.LoadSaveGameData` makes, so every TAOM CampaignBehavior, `SyncData`, `[SaveableProperty]` and definer round-trips normally. The real gate is the join handshake: `ModuleValidator.Validate` demands (1) identical game version, (2) zero DLC modules on the client, (3) every non-official server module present on the client at an EXACTLY equal version including ChangeSet, and (4) zero client modules the server doesn't have. Nothing is hashed — no assembly checksum, no ModuleData content check — so TAOM is allowed to be present, but only if the host and every client run a byte-identical module set declared at identical `SubModule.xml` versions. TAOM's own work is small: teach `CoopPresence` the module id "Coop" (a one-line `coop-modules.txt` edit), and accept that data-only divergence between players is undetectable and will desync silently.

findings.claim: NO save-definer collision. BannerlordCoop declares exactly two SaveableTypeDefiners in the entire decompiled tree, claiming base ids 44177000 and 44182000. TAOM's 726900501/601/701/801 are ~682,000,000 away. Coop's AutoSyncExport (43 generated files shipped by the mod) contains zero SaveableTypeDefiner. No engine ArgumentException is possible from this pairing.
findings.taom_impact: Nothing. TAOM's four definers can stay exactly as they are. TAOM's existing SaveDefinerCollisionGuard preflight (Main/Features/CoopInterop/SaveDefinerCollisionGuard.cs, run from Main/SubModule.cs:126) will report clean when Coop is loaded. Do NOT renumber anything.

findings.claim: THE HARD GATE: the join handshake requires the client's active module list to be EXACTLY equal to the server's for every non-official module, with version equality checked INCLUDING ChangeSet, plus a symmetric 'server does not support module X' rejection for any extra client module. TAOM, TAOM.Dependencies, TAOM_Map, LOTRLOME_Armory and the four BUTR alias stubs must all be present on both sides at identical declared versions.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must ship an identical module set to host and clients. TAOM's SubModule.xml Version is v2.0.15 and Dependencies is v2.0.5 — those strings, not the DLL contents, are what is compared, so bumping one side's version string without the other breaks joins. Document a 'all players run the same TAOM release' requirement; there is no partial-mod-match mode.

findings.claim: Modules are enumerated with ModuleHelper.GetActiveModules() and reduced to (Id, IsOfficial, IsDlc, Version). Nothing else is transmitted: no assembly hash, no file checksum, no ModuleData digest, no DLL version.
findings.taom_impact: POSITIVE for presence (TAOM is never rejected for being unknown), NEGATIVE for safety: two players can run the SAME declared TAOM version with divergent troops.xml / spcultures.xml / item defs and join successfully, then desync on any object the host references and the client cannot resolve. If TAOM wants protection it must add its own content-hash exchange (e.g. a TAOM console command or a hash written into save metadata) — Coop provides none.

findings.claim: Any DLC module on the client is a hard rejection, checked before the module-list comparison.

Note the Coop server-instructions doc independently tells users to 'Disable Warsails DLL if you have it'.

findings.claim: Game version is validated by taking the FIRST IsOfficial module in each list and comparing versions with checkChangeSet:false. TAOM declares ModuleType Community (not official) so it is never mistaken for the version anchor.

If TAOM ever flipped to Official it could become the version anchor AND be skipped by ShouldValidateModule (official non-DLC modules are excluded from the per-module check), silently disabling TAOM version matching. Add this to the engine-bump checklist.

All TAOM SaveableTypeDefiners, SyncData and LoadInitializationCallbacks run normally. dimension: GameModel and CampaignBehavior handling — do TAOM's overrides survive BannerlordCoop?
summary: BannerlordCoop registers zero GameModels and removes zero: its NoHarmony `AddModel`/`ReplaceModel`/`RemoveModel`/`ReplaceBehavior` machinery exists but is never called, `CoopMod.NoHarmonyLoad()` queues no model tasks, and the only `CampaignGameStarter` interaction is `AddBehavior` of two Coop behaviors. Nothing type-scans `gameStarter.Models` or the `CampaignBehaviorManager`, so all ~30 TAOM GameModel overrides and all 31 TAOM `CampaignBehaviorBase` subclasses register and stay registered — load order is irrelevant to this dimension. Coop instead Harmony-patches 15 concrete `Default*Model` types and ~150 vanilla `CampaignBehavior` types by hardcoded `typeof(...)`; because every TAOM model override calls `base.X(...)` and targets different methods (or the same method whose replacement re-routes through `Campaign.Current.Models`), the two overlapping full-replacements — `DefaultPartyWageModel.GetTotalWage` and `DefaultClanFinanceModel.CalculateClanIncomeInternal` — still dispatch back into TAOM's model. The real damage is indirect: ~19 vanilla behaviours that consume TAOM models are prefixed to `return false` (2 unconditionally: Aging, Pregnancy; the rest client-only), so those TAOM models become inert on clients, and TAOM's own 31 behaviours have no server/client gate and will double-apply state mutations on every client.

findings.claim: BannerlordCoop registers, replaces, or removes NO GameModel. The NoHarmony model-manipulation API exists but is never invoked anywhere in the mod — `CoopMod.NoHarmonyLoad()` only adds two InitialStateOptions, so `ModelDelegates` is empty when `NoHarmonyLoader.OnGameStart` iterates it.
findings.taom_impact: Nothing. All ~30 TAOM GameModel registrations survive verbatim; there is no load-order fix needed because there is nothing to lose a race against. A repo-wide grep for `ReplaceModel|RemoveModel|ReplaceBehavior|.AddModel(|AddModel<` returns only the unused NoHarmonyLoader definitions.

findings.claim: Coop's only `CampaignGameStarter` mutation is two `AddBehavior` calls, made unconditionally in EVERY campaign — including a pure single-player TAOM game with no coop session running.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must accept two extra behaviours in every save while the Coop module is enabled. Both have empty `SyncData(IDataStore)`, so no new save fields. Two `start`-token dialog lines are added at priority 10000 (above every TAOM dialog); their conditions call `IsPhase(...)` which returns false when `PlayerPartyInteractionDialogState.Phase` is `None`, so they never fire in SP — but `IsPhase` unconditionally runs `MBTextManager.SetTextVariable("COOP_PLAYER_PARTY_INTERACTION_TEXT", ...)` on every conversation evaluation. Harmless; note it if a TAOM dialog ever reads that variable name.

findings.claim: Coop never sweeps behaviours or models by type-scan. Every disable is a Harmony prefix on a hardcoded `typeof(VanillaBehavior)`'s `RegisterEvents`, and Harmony discovery is scoped to Coop's own assembly.
findings.taom_impact: None of TAOM's 31 `CampaignBehaviorBase` subclasses can be stripped — they are unknown types to Coop. Verified TAOM has no behaviour deriving from a vanilla `*CampaignBehavior` (a grep for behaviour class declarations not inheriting `CampaignBehaviorBase` returns only BehaviorTree/AgentComponent types), so no TAOM behaviour inherits a prefixed `RegisterEvents`.

findings.claim: None of Coop's patching applies in single-player. `GameInterface.PatchAll()` — which installs every Disable patch and the AutoSync transpilers — is only reached from the coop client's `MainMenuState.Handle_NetworkConnected` and from `CoopartiveMultiplayerExperience`'s server start.
findings.taom_impact: Merely installing the Coop module alongside TAOM does not perturb TAOM's models or behaviours. All findings below apply only inside an active coop session. TAOM does not need a "Coop present" kill-switch; it needs a "coop session active + which role" gate.

findings.claim: Coop Harmony-patches 15 concrete vanilla model types. Seven overlap TAOM's registry: DefaultPartyWageModel, DefaultClanFinanceModel, DefaultArmyManagementCalculationModel, DefaultMobilePartyFoodConsumptionModel, DefaultPartyMoraleModel, DefaultPartySizeLimitModel, DefaultPartySpeedCalculatingModel.
findings.taom_impact: Patching the base class is what SAVES TAOM here: `TaomPartySizeModel : DefaultPartySizeLimitModel` overrides `GetPartyMemberSizeLimit` and calls `base.GetPartyMemberSizeLimit(...)`, so Coop's prefix on the inner `CalculateMobilePartyMemberSizeLimit` still fires (it only short-circuits for player-owned caravans). Same shape for TaomPartySpeedModel (overrides `CalculateFinalSpeed`, Coop postfixes `CalculateBaseSpeed`), TaomFoodConsumptionModel (overrides `CalculateDailyFoodConsumptionf`, Coop prefixes `DoesPartyConsumeFood`), TaomArmyManagementModel (overrides `DailyBeingAtArmyInfluenceAward`/`CalculatePartyInfluenceCost`, Coop prefixes `CheckPartyEligibility`), TaomPartyMoraleModel (overrides `GetEffectivePartyMorale` calling base; Coop's null-HomeSettlement militia guard on the base still applies). No method-level collision. TAOM must preserve the `base.X()` call in every one of these — dropping it is what would silently disable Coop's sync.

findings.claim: Coop fully replaces `DefaultPartyWageModel.GetTotalWage` (prefix returns false) with a hand-copied reimplementation — but that copy computes per-troop wage via `character.TroopWage`, which the engine routes back through `Campaign.Current.Models.PartyWageModel.GetCharacterWage`, i.e. through TAOM's model.

				num += num10;
findings.taom_impact: TaomPartyWageModel's T0-T10 tier wage table (`GetCharacterWage`) survives: `E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/.../CharacterObject.cs:349` reads `return Campaign.Current.Models.PartyWageModel.GetCharacterWage(this);`. TaomPartyWageModel.GetTotalWage's own culture/career post-processing also survives because it runs AFTER `base.GetTotalWage(...)` returns Coop's value. The loss is narrow: Coop's copy is a snapshot of vanilla v1.4.7 `GetTotalWage`, so if TaleWorlds changes that body in a future patch the coop path silently diverges. TAOM does not need to change anything here, but should not add logic to the vanilla body's path expecting it to run.

findings.claim: Coop fully replaces `DefaultClanFinanceModel.CalculateClanIncomeInternal` and `AddExpenseFromLeaderParty`/`AddPartyExpense` (all prefixes returning false), but the income replacement calls `model.AddSettlementIncome(...)`, whose vanilla body dispatches tariffs through `Campaign.Current.Models.ClanFinanceModel`.
findings.taom_impact: TaomClanFinanceModel's only override, `CalculateTownIncomeFromTariffs` (Umbar tariff feat), still fires — the vanilla engine at `E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/.../DefaultClanFinanceModel.cs:404` reads `Campaign.Current.Models.ClanFinanceModel.CalculateTownIncomeFromTariffs(clan, fief, applyWithdrawals);`, a virtual dispatch onto TAOM's registered instance. No TAOM change needed. If TAOM ever overrides `CalculateClanIncomeInternal`, `AddExpenseFromLeaderParty`, `AddPartyExpense`, or `CalculateClanExpensesInternal` directly, that override is bypassed under coop.

findings.claim: Two vanilla behaviours are disabled UNCONDITIONALLY (server and client alike): AgingCampaignBehavior and PregnancyCampaignBehavior. Both are the sole tick-drivers for the models TAOM overrides for race lifespans and race pregnancy durations.
findings.taom_impact: TaomAgeModel and TaomPregnancyModel remain REGISTERED and are still read for static thresholds (`Models.AgeModel.HeroComesOfAge` etc. are queried elsewhere), but the aging progression and pregnancy tick that consume them stop entirely inside any coop session. Verified: AgingCampaignBehavior references `Campaign.Current.Models.AgeModel` 10 times; PregnancyCampaignBehavior calls `Campaign.Current.Models.PregnancyModel.GetDailyChanceOfPregnancyForHero` and `.PregnancyDurationInDays`. TAOM's elven-immortality/dwarf-aging and race pregnancy features are dead in coop. Fix requires TAOM to reimplement the tick in its own behaviour (which Coop cannot disable) or accept the loss. Same unconditional treatment hits BattleCampaignBehavior, EducationCampaignBehavior, HeirSelectionCampaignBehavior, DynamicBodyCampaignBehavior, MarriageOfferCampaignBehavior, ClanMemberRolesCampaignBehavior, CrimeCampaignBehavior, RetirementCampaignBehavior, IssuesCampaignBehavior, GuardsCampaignBehavior, ArenaMasterCampaignBehavior, NPCEquipmentsCampaignBehavior, PrisonerRecruitCampaignBehavior and ~40 issue/quest behaviours.

findings.claim: A further ~40 vanilla behaviours are disabled CLIENT-side only via `return ModInformation.IsServer;` on RegisterEvents. Several are the exclusive consumers of TAOM GameModels.
findings.taom_impact: This is architecturally CORRECT for TAOM — the server keeps running these, so TaomSettlementMilitiaModel (MilitiasCampaignBehavior), TaomVillageProductionModel (VillageGoodProductionCampaignBehavior), TaomSettlementProsperityModel / TaomSettlementLoyaltyModel / TaomSettlementFoodModel (SettlementVariablesBehavior), TaomPartyTroopUpgradeModel (PartyUpgraderCampaignBehavior), TaomVolunteerModel (RecruitmentCampaignBehavior), TaomTournamentModel (TournamentCampaignBehavior), TaomFoodConsumptionModel (FoodConsumptionBehavior), TaomSettlementEconomyModel (TradeCampaignBehavior) all still compute — on the host only, with results replicated. The requirement is that TAOM must never rely on these behaviours firing on a client for UI/state it draws locally.

findings.claim: `AiVisitSettlementBehavior.RegisterEvents` is client-disabled, which makes TAOM's two riskiest transpilers dead code on clients.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM's `Patch42_AiHourlyTick_Transpiler` (`AccessTools.Method(typeof(AiVisitSettlementBehavior), "AiHourlyTick")`) and `Patch42_FillSettlements_Transpiler` (`FillSettlementsToVisitWithDistancesAsDays`) still INSTALL cleanly — Coop patches a different method, so no transpiler conflict — but the transpiled methods are never invoked client-side. CastleRecruitment is host-authoritative under coop, which is correct. Same for `Main/Features/ArmyTargeting/Hooks/AiMilitaryBehavior_CalculateDistanceScoreForBesieging_Patch.cs` and TaomTargetScoreModel (Coop patches no TargetScoreCalculatingModel at all — grep returns nothing). No TAOM change required; document the expectation.

findings.claim: THE ACTIONABLE GAP: TAOM's 31 CampaignBehaviors have no server/client role gate, so they run identically on host and clients. Coop's roster interception detects and logs this but does not block it — the client's local mutation proceeds and then diverges from the replicated authoritative state.
findings.taom_impact: Concrete case: `Main/Features/AlignmentDesertion/Hooks/AlignmentDesertionBehavior.cs:34` subscribes `CampaignEvents.DailyTickPartyEvent` and line 122 calls `roster.AddToCounts(character, -toRemove)`. The engine's `AddToCounts` funnels to `AddToCountsAtIndex` (`E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/.../TroopRoster.cs:453`), so on the SERVER the mutation is published as `CountsAtIndexAdded` and replicates correctly; on the CLIENT the prefix is `void` — it logs an error and lets the mutation through, double-applying the desertion locally. TAOM must add a coop-role gate (an `ITaomCoopRole` service reading Coop's `Common.ModInformation.IsServer` by reflection, or a Coop-session probe) and early-return from every state-mutating campaign tick on clients. Apply to AlignmentDesertion first, then audit all 31 behaviours for `DailyTick*`/`HourlyTick*` mutations.

findings.claim: `AllowDefaultPartyDesertionModel` is a thread-local sync WHITELIST, not a model replacement — it brackets the desertion query so its scratch-roster writes are not treated as authoritative game-state mutations.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM overrides no PartyDesertionModel, so there is zero direct conflict. The mechanism matters though: `E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/.../DefaultPartyDesertionModel.cs:35` builds `TroopRoster.CreateDummyTroopRoster()` and populates it, and the AllowedThread window stops that scratch write tripping the replication path. If TAOM ever builds a scratch TroopRoster inside a model or service under coop, it must do the same (`Common.Util.AllowedThread`) or its scratch writes will be published to clients as real roster changes. Note also that TAOM's AlignmentDesertion is entirely separate from vanilla `DesertionCampaignBehavior`, which Coop client-disables — so TAOM's desertion is the only one running client-side today.

findings.claim: Coop's tournament UI gate is an exact-type check on `FightTournamentGame`, which TAOM currently passes.
findings.taom_impact: `TaomTournamentModel : DefaultTournamentModel` (Main/Features/Arena/Models/TaomTournamentModel.cs) overrides only GetTournamentStartChance/GetTournamentEndChance/GetRegularRewardItems/GetEliteRewardItems/GetParticipantArmor and does NOT override tournament-game creation — a grep for `FightTournamentGame` across `Main/` returns nothing. So coop tournaments stay enabled. Standing constraint: TAOM must never introduce a `FightTournamentGame` subclass, or every coop tournament silently degrades to the "unsupported" tooltip.

findings.taom_impact: Verified shared types and their disjoint methods: DefaultPartySizeLimitModel (TAOM: `FindAppropriateInitialRosterForMobileParty`; Coop: `CalculateMobilePartyMemberSizeLimit` + `GetInitialPartySizeRatioForMobileParty`), PartyUpgraderCampaignBehavior (TAOM: `UpgradeReadyTroops`; Coop: `RegisterEvents`), HideoutCampaignBehavior (TAOM: `game_menu_hideout_place_on_init`; Coop: `RegisterEvents`), CaravansCampaignBehavior (TAOM: 4 internals; Coop: `RegisterEvents`), CampaignBehaviorManager (TAOM: `LoadBehaviorData`; Coop: no patch). No TAOM change needed, but this is a standing regression check: if TAOM ever adds a PREFIX to a method Coop also prefixes-and-returns-false, TAOM's prefix is skipped.

integration_api.how_taom_uses_it: The single source of truth Coop itself uses for every server/client branch: `public static bool IsServer { get; set; } = false;` and `public static bool IsClient => !IsServer;`. TAOM's coop-role gate should read this (via reflection, to avoid a hard assembly reference on Common.dll) and early-return from client-side state-mutating campaign ticks. Caveat: it defaults to `false` (=IsClient) even when no coop session exists, so TAOM must AND it with a session-active probe — see ContainerProvider below — or a pure-SP TAOM run would be misdetected as a client.
integration_api.is_public: public static class, public static properties

integration_api.how_taom_uses_it: `public static bool TryGetContainer(out ILifetimeScope lifetimeScope)` returns false until `SetContainer` runs at coop start. This is the cheapest reflection-friendly "is a coop session live?" probe — combine with ModInformation.IsServer to derive the three states TAOM needs (SP / coop-host / coop-client). Do NOT rely on the `Alive` property: it is initialised once at static-ctor time (`public static bool Alive { get; } = _lifetimeScope != null;`) and is therefore permanently false.

integration_api.how_taom_uses_it: `AllowThisThread()` / `RevokeThisThread()` / `IsThisThreadAllowed()` (thread-static counter) plus `IDisposable Suspend()`. If a TAOM GameModel or service builds a scratch TroopRoster/ItemRoster the way `DefaultPartyDesertionModel.GetTroopsToDesert` does, TAOM must bracket it exactly as `AllowDefaultPartyDesertionModel` does, or its scratch writes get published to clients as real state changes.

integration_api.how_taom_uses_it: `public static bool IsOriginalAllowed()` is the gate every roster/state patch consults; it returns true when AllowedThread is open OR when the sync policy says so (`ServerSyncPolicy.AllowOriginal() => !(serverLogic.State is ServerRunningState)`, `ClientSyncPolicy` returns false in CampaignState/MissionState). Read-only reference for TAOM: it tells you exactly when a TAOM mutation will be replicated versus treated as a desync.

dimension: Object manager and identity — does TAOM's custom XML content survive BannerlordCoop's id scheme?
summary: BannerlordCoop keys every networked object by the string `"{TypeName}_{StringId}"`, built independently on each peer by walking the live object graph after the campaign is ready — not by MBGUID, not by load-order index. That is excellent news for TAOM: hundreds of custom cultures/troops/items/settlements defined in XML resolve correctly on both peers with zero coop-side work, because coop never assigns them ids of its own. The client additionally loads the *server's actual save file* (`SaveManager.Load` over an in-memory driver), so the campaign object graph is the server's by construction; only MBObjectManager XML objects come from local ModuleData. There is NO data validation beyond module id + `ApplicationVersion` (incl. changeset) — no hash, no checksum, no manifest anywhere in the tree — so divergent TAOM ModuleData is undetected and degrades silently: unresolved ids return `null` (`BinaryPackageBase.ResolveObject`) or drop the write (`GenericHandler`), with two known throwing sites. The blockers are TAOM's own behavior, not coop's identity model: TAOM creates Heroes at runtime on BOTH peers (CastleRecruitment `OnGameLoaded` + `OnDailyTickSettlement`, CultureConversion `DailyTick`), and coop's contract is that only the server may create managed objects — a client-side `new Hero()` is merely logged as an error, never registered, and its `StringId` assignment is silently suppressed by a patch on the `MBObjectBase.StringId` setter. Secondary hazard: `EquipmentRegistry` keys equipment by ordinal position inside each `MBEquipmentRoster`, making TAOM's equipmentset XML *ordering* load-bearing across peers.

findings.claim: Coop's object identity is `"{TypeName}_{StringId}"`, derived independently on each peer from the live object graph. TAOM's XML content therefore needs no coop-side registration — StringId equality is the entire contract.
findings.taom_impact: POSITIVE. TAOM does not need to register anything with coop. Every custom culture/troop/item/settlement resolves as long as both peers' ModuleData produces identical StringIds. Guard this by making the TAOM ModuleData tree byte-identical on host and client (it already must be, for the vanilla save-load below).

findings.claim: Every XML-backed type TAOM extends is registered by StringId out of MBObjectManager / the campaign collections — CultureObject, CharacterObject, ItemObject, Settlement, PartyTemplateObject all use `RegisterExistingObject(x.StringId, x)`.
findings.taom_impact: POSITIVE. TAOM's ~hundreds of XML cultures/troops/items/settlements are picked up automatically. No MBObjectBase subclass and no RegisterType call is needed — which matches TAOM's data-driven design exactly.

findings.claim: MBGUID is NOT used for cross-peer identity anywhere. The only reference to it is a legacy binary-package wrapper. Load-order-derived `MBObjectBase.Id` values never cross the wire.
findings.evidence_quote: public class MBGUIDBinaryPackage : BinaryPackageBase<MBGUID>
findings.taom_impact: POSITIVE. TAOM does not need to control module load order for id determinism. The MBGUID counter (`obj.Id = GetNewId()` in the engine's MBObjectManager.RegisterObject) can differ freely between peers.

findings.claim: The client loads the SERVER's save file, so the runtime campaign graph is the server's. Only XML-defined MBObjects come from local ModuleData — the standard vanilla "save references content you don't have" failure applies before coop ever gets involved.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM's 4 SaveableTypeDefiners and all its ModuleData must be identical on both peers, because the client runs a full vanilla load of the host's save. A ModuleData mismatch produces a vanilla load fault, which TAOM's SaveShield would surface — this is the earliest and loudest divergence detector available; do not suppress it in coop sessions.

findings.claim: TAOM creates Heroes on the CLIENT at game-load time. `CastleRecruitmentBehavior.OnGameLoaded` runs during the client's load of the host save (before coop's `CampaignReady`/registration), so the client ends up with notables the server does not have.
findings.taom_impact: BLOCKER. Must gate on "am I a coop client" and skip. Ordering is proven: coop publishes `CampaignReady` from a `MapScreen.OnInitialize` postfix, and `LoadingState.Handle_CampaignLoaded` calls `RegisterAllGameObjects()` only then — so TAOM's OnGameLoaded heroes are already in `CampaignObjectManager` and get registered under locally-derived ids the server has never heard of.

findings.claim: TAOM creates Heroes on the CLIENT every campaign day. The client advances its own map clock (server-corrected), coop disables only a curated list of ~134 vanilla behaviors' `RegisterEvents`, and TAOM's behaviors are not in that list — so `OnDailyTickSettlement` → `TickCastle` → `HeroCreator.CreateNotable` fires client-side.
findings.taom_impact: BLOCKER. Same for `CultureConversionBehavior`'s `CampaignEvents.DailyTickEvent` → `ReplaceNotable` → `HeroCreator.CreateNotable` (Main/Adapters/CultureConversionAdapter.cs:152). Both must be server-only. There is no generic tick suppression in coop to save you — coop's client clock is live (`CampaignTimePacingPatches` postfixes `Campaign.TickMapTime` and calls `ApplyClientSimulationTime`).

findings.claim: A client that creates a managed type is only LOGGED, never blocked and never registered. The object becomes a permanent orphan invisible to the network layer.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM gets no exception and no visible symptom — just a Serilog error and permanent state divergence. TAOM must self-police: every runtime object-creation site needs an explicit "server or single-player only" gate. Note the prefix fires for `HeroCreator.CreateNotable` too, because `Hero(string, CharacterObject, CampaignTime, CampaignTime)` chains `: this()` to the parameterless ctor that `HeroRegistry.Constructors` patches.

findings.claim: Coop prefixes the `MBObjectBase.StringId` setter and returns false (skip original) outside an allowed window. A client-side `new Hero(stringId, ...)` therefore keeps a null StringId — the engine's `base.StringId = FindNextUniqueStringId<Hero>(stringId)` is silently dropped — and that null-id Hero is still added to `CampaignObjectManager`.
findings.taom_impact: Any TAOM code that creates or renames an MBObjectBase during a live coop session is neutered — on BOTH peers, since `ServerSyncPolicy.AllowOriginal()` also returns false during `ServerRunningState`. Server-side creation of the 43 managed types still works because coop assigns `Created_{n}` inside an `AllowedThread`; anything else just loses its id. TAOM must not assume `StringId` assignment sticks in a coop session.

findings.claim: Equipment ids are ORDINAL, not StringId-based: `{roster.StringId}_{index}` over `MBEquipmentRoster.AllEquipments`. A one-element ordering/count difference in TAOM's equipmentset XML silently remaps every later equipment in that roster to the WRONG object.
findings.taom_impact: HIGH and easy to miss. TAOM's `equipmentsets/` XML (and any XSLT that emits `<EquipmentSet>` elements) must produce identical ordering on both peers, not merely identical content. This is the one place where "same data, different order" produces silent corruption rather than a missing-object error. Worth a validator in tools/ that hashes the ordered equipment-set list per roster.

findings.claim: There is NO game-data validation. The join handshake validates only module id + `ApplicationVersion` (with changeset) and forbids DLC. Grepping the whole tree for checksum/SHA/MD5/manifest returns nothing.
findings.taom_impact: Two peers running TAOM v2.0.13 with different ModuleData (a local XML tweak, a partially-updated Workshop download, a hand-edited troops file) pass validation and then diverge silently. If TAOM wants safety it must add its own ModuleData content hash — there is no coop hook for it, so it would have to ride on TAOM's own channel or simply be surfaced in-game as a warning. Note the validator is also strictly symmetric: any module the *client* has that the server lacks is rejected too, so LOTRLOME_Armory / TAOM_Map / TAOM.Dependencies must match exactly on both sides.

findings.claim: An unresolvable id fails SOFT everywhere on the hot path: the receive handler logs a Serilog error and skips the write; the send side suppresses the entire message when a referenced value has no id.
findings.taom_impact: No crash, but no recovery either — the peers drift apart with only a log line. TAOM cannot rely on a hard failure to detect content mismatch. Any TAOM coop-compat QA pass must scrape the coop Serilog output for `Failed to get {name} using {id}` rather than waiting for a CTD.

findings.claim: Binary-package deserialization of an unknown object id returns `null` with no log at all — quieter than the handler path.
findings.taom_impact: If a joining player's hero wears a TAOM item the host lacks, the item silently becomes `null` inside the unpacked `Equipment`, and the NRE surfaces much later in unrelated engine code. This is the worst-case debugging shape for TAOM — argues for a TAOM-side ModuleData hash warning at join time rather than trusting coop's handshake.

findings.claim: Two sites DO throw on an unresolved id, and one of them is squarely in TAOM territory: tournament bracket hydration keyed on `CharacterObject` ids.
findings.taom_impact: A TAOM troop CharacterObject present on the host but not the client turns a tournament into a hard NRE. TAOM's tournament-related content (custom contestant troops) is therefore the highest-risk content divergence surface — test tournaments explicitly in any coop bring-up.

findings.claim: Server-side runtime creation IS handled and works: the server rewrites the new object's StringId to `Created_{n}` inside an allowed window, registers it, and broadcasts a create message; the client builds a constructor-skipped shell with the same id.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM's runtime hero creation is viable IF it is server-only. Consequence to accept: the created hero's StringId will be `Created_N`, NOT the template-derived id vanilla would have given it. Any TAOM code that parses or pattern-matches a runtime hero's StringId (or persists it) will misbehave in coop sessions.

findings.claim: The client's sanctioned hero-creation path is character creation, where the client builds the hero locally *outside* the sync states and the SERVER assigns the authoritative ids on unpack.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM features that hook character creation (race selection, InitialChildGeneration, culture-specific starting kit) run on the client during `CharacterCreationState`, where `ClientSyncPolicy.AllowOriginal()` is TRUE — so they execute unpatched and their results survive via the binary package. That is the one client-side creation path TAOM can safely keep. Everything it touches must be resolvable by StringId on the host.

findings.claim: The sync policy is state-scoped, not peer-scoped: original engine behavior runs freely on the client during loading and character creation, and is only intercepted once the client enters `CampaignState`/`MissionState`.
findings.taom_impact: Explains why TAOM's `OnGameLoaded` hero creation is the nastier of the two blockers: it runs UNGATED (no error log, no StringId suppression), producing fully-formed client-only heroes that then get registered as if legitimate. The daily-tick path at least leaves a `Client created managed Hero` error in the log. TAOM's server-only gate must therefore be its own check, not a reliance on coop refusing the call.

findings.claim: The server ships a derived-id → server-id remap with the save so the client's independent re-derivation lands on the server's ids. Client-only objects get no entry.
findings.taom_impact: Confirms the design intent: the server's object set is authoritative and the client's registration is reconciled against it. TAOM objects that exist only on the client fall outside this reconciliation entirely — and if their derived id happens to collide with a server id, `ObjectManager.AddExisting` logs "Duplicate id" and leaves the object unregistered.

findings.claim: TAOM's co-op detection does not recognise this mod. `CoopPresence` matches only "BannerlordTogether" and "BattleLinkMPClient"; the module id here is "Coop".
findings.taom_impact: Cheapest fix in the whole analysis, and a prerequisite for every gate above. Add "Coop" to `CompiledModuleDefaults` (or ship it in `coop-modules.txt`, which the loader already unions in). Coop's Harmony owner ids are now known from the decompile and can go in `ExtraProtectedOwnerPrefixes`: "Bannerlord.Coop" (GameInterfaceModule.cs:41), "CoopAutoRegistryFactory" (AutoRegistryFactory.cs:18), "Coop.BootFix", "Coop.UILoading".

findings.claim: Coop exposes per-type object auditors as debug console commands that diff the client's object set against the server's — a ready-made divergence detector, but manual only, never automatic.
findings.taom_impact: USE THIS. The hero-count-mismatch audit is exactly the assertion that catches TAOM's client-side CreateNotable bug. Any TAOM coop bring-up should run the hero / mobileparty / settlement audit console commands after a few in-game days as the acceptance test for the server-only gates.

open_questions: Does the client's `MapScreen.OnInitialize` (which publishes `CampaignReady`) always fire AFTER `CampaignEvents.OnGameLoadedEvent`? The ordering is strongly implied by the load pipeline (`SaveManager.Load` → `SandBoxGameManager(loadResult)` → campaign load → map screen init) and by the fact that coop's registration must see a fully-loaded campaign, but I did not trace the engine's state-machine transition to prove it. If the order were reversed, TAOM's OnGameLoaded heroes would be created AFTER registration and would be unregistered rather than mis-registered — different symptom, same divergence.

What exactly does a client-created `Hero` with a suppressed (null) StringId do to a later save on the client? The client never saves in coop, but `SaveGameHandler`/`CoopSaveManager` exist server-side — NOT INVESTIGATED whether a client can ever be asked to serialize its own graph.

`EnsureNextUniqueIdAbove` bumps a per-type counter from any registered id whose trailing `_<digits>` parses as an int. Whether any TAOM StringId ends in `_<number>` densely enough to matter is not checked, but the counter only feeds server-side `Created_{n}` id generation, so a collision would need a TAOM object literally named `Created_<n>` — NOT FOUND, but not exhaustively grepped against TAOM's ModuleData.

Do TAOM's XSLT transforms guarantee stable element ordering within `MBEquipmentRoster.AllEquipments`? The ordinal-keyed EquipmentRegistry makes this load-bearing, and XSLT output ordering was not audited here.

Whether `MBEquipmentRoster` iteration order (`Campaign.Current.AllEquipmentRosters`) affects anything — it does not affect the id (ids are scoped per roster StringId), but I did not verify that two rosters can never share a StringId in TAOM's data.

dimension: Mission/battle sync — do TAOM's custom creatures and combat survive BannerlordCoop?
summary: BannerlordCoop battles use distributed authority, not a single simulator: each peer owns the agents it spawned and every other peer holds a `Controller = AgentControllerType.None` "puppet" copy driven by position/action packets. Damage is not recomputed — the attacking peer computes the blow with its own GameModels and MBRandom rolls and ships the fully-resolved `Blow` + `AttackCollisionData` over the wire, which the victim's owner replays via `Agent.RegisterBlow`. That design is unusually friendly to TAOM: puppet spawn resolves `CharacterObject` by StringId and lets `AgentData` default `AgentMonster = FaceGen.GetBaseMonsterFromRace(AgentRace)`, so TAOM races/monsters/skeletons and creature mounts materialize with zero coop-side changes; `MonsterRegistry` enumerates `MBObjectManager.GetObjectTypeList<Monster>()` by StringId; the coop launchers still go through `MissionState.OpenNew`, so every TAOM `MissionLogic` (including `BehaviorTreeMissionLogic`) is still added by the engine's submodule hook, and `CoopMissionController` declares `MissionBehaviorType.Other` so it does not trip TAOM's MissionLogic-cast regression. The blocker is on TAOM's side: TAOM's creature attacks are behavior-tree driven, attach to **every** matching agent in `Mission.Current.AllAgents` with no ownership concept, and call the private `Mission.RegisterBlow` directly — and coop's only attacker-ownership gates (`MeleeHitCallbackPatch`, `ChargeDamageCallbackPatch`, `AgentDamagePatch`) live in the `Missions` assembly **uncategorized and therefore never applied**. Every peer independently rolls and emits a trample/bite/spider-crit for the same creature, so creature damage multiplies by the peer count with divergent rolls. Secondary breakage: creature-mount action channels are never replicated (mounts are skipped by the action handler), and TAOM's per-tick `TeleportToPosition` / `SetScriptedPositionAndDirection` creature control fights coop's `AgentPositionInterpolator` on puppets. Hideout missions have no coop entry point at all (NOT FOUND).

findings.claim: BLOCKER — TAOM's BT-driven creature attacks are ownership-blind and coop applies no attacker gate on Mission.RegisterBlow, so every peer independently rolls and emits the same creature attack. Damage multiplies by peer count with divergent MBRandom rolls.
findings.evidence_quote: int count = _tracker.AttachAll(Mission.Current.AllAgents);
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must add an ownership gate before any BT attack task fires a blow. Dependency-free version: skip when the creature (or its RiderAgent for mounts) has `Controller == AgentControllerType.None`, since PuppetSpawner assigns None to all remotely-owned agents. Stronger version: soft-resolve `Missions.INetworkAgentRegistry.IsLocallyControlled(Agent)` by reflection when the Coop module is loaded. Applies to ElephantLikeAttackTasks, SpiderAttackService, MumakilCombat, and the warg bite path.

findings.claim: Coop's attacker-ownership gates for melee/charge/fall/area damage exist in source but are NEVER APPLIED: GameInterface.PatchAll() runs PatchAllUncategorized only on the GameInterface assembly, and the Missions assembly is patched solely through two registered categories ('CoopMissilePatches', 'CoopAgentVoicePatches'). AgentDamagePatch / MeleeHitCallbackPatch / ChargeDamageCallbackPatch / RegisterBlowPatch carry no category attribute.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM cannot rely on Coop suppressing duplicate attacker-side damage. The only live interception is BattleBlowInterceptPatch on Agent.RegisterBlow, which gates on the VICTIM being a puppet, never on the attacker. TAOM owns the whole de-duplication problem for any damage it originates outside the engine's weapon-collision callbacks.

findings.claim: TAOM's synthetic creature blows DO reach coop's interception (so they are routed, not silently dropped) — CustomAttacksUtils calls the private Mission.RegisterBlow, which calls victim.RegisterBlow, which BattleBlowInterceptPatch prefixes. TAOM passes _isColliderAgent: true, which is the branch that reaches victim.RegisterBlow.
findings.evidence_quote: victim.RegisterBlow(b, in collisionData);
findings.taom_impact: Good news half of the blocker: once TAOM adds the ownership gate, creature damage against another player's troops WILL replicate correctly with no further work — the blow arrives pre-resolved (DamageCalculated = true) and is replayed verbatim by the owner.

findings.claim: Puppet spawn never sets a Monster on AgentBuildData; the engine defaults it from the character's race. TAOM's custom races therefore resolve to TAOM's custom Monster/skeleton automatically on remote peers.
findings.taom_impact: No TAOM action required for creature identity. Confirmed against E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/Core/TaleWorlds.Core/TaleWorlds.Core/AgentData.cs:61 `AgentMonster = FaceGen.GetBaseMonsterFromRace(AgentRace);`. TAOM must only guarantee identical monsters.xml / races on both peers.

findings.claim: Coop's non-human == mount assumption in the blow interceptor is safe for TAOM only because TAOM's humanoid creatures declare IsHumanoid="true". Any future TAOM combatant that is non-humanoid AND non-mount would be routed through the mount-authority branch.
findings.taom_impact: Keep IsHumanoid="true" on every walking TAOM combatant monster (hill_troll/cave_troll already do, per docs/reference/lotrlome-armory-snapshot/monsters.xml:869 `IsHumanoid="true"`). Add a data-validation check so a future creature cannot ship non-humanoid-and-non-mount.

findings.claim: Creature-mount attack animations will not replicate: the action handler skips every agent with IsMount, so a mumakil/warg/spider's SetActionChannel-driven attack clips are never sent. Only each peer's own locally-run behavior tree animates it.
findings.taom_impact: Once TAOM gates BT attacks to the owner only, remote peers will see creature mounts with NO attack animation (damage arrives with no visible trample). TAOM needs its own lightweight animation-replication path for creature mounts, or must accept cosmetic desync. Non-mount creatures (trolls) are unaffected — they are IsHuman and their action channels replicate.

findings.claim: Action replication is index-based on the wire: the sender transmits the raw animation code and the RECEIVER resolves it through native IMBAnimation.GetActionNameWithCode. Divergent module/animation load order between peers silently maps a TAOM creature action to the wrong clip.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM must enforce identical module set AND identical load order across peers (TAOM + LOTRLOME_Armory + all animation-contributing modules). A version/load-order handshake at session join is worth adding — TAOM already owns action_types drift detection (MumakilCombat.Profile.AnyUnresolved()); extend it to a cross-peer checksum.

findings.claim: Puppets are moved by coop's interpolator via SetTargetPositionAndDirection / TeleportToPosition every tick. TAOM's creature behaviors drive the same agents with TeleportToPosition and SetScriptedPositionAndDirection every tick on all peers, so the two controllers fight on remote copies.
findings.taom_impact: The same ownership gate needed for attacks must also wrap TAOM's movement writes: WargAiControlledGetToEnemy.cs:36 (`warg.RiderAgent.SetScriptedPositionAndDirection(...)`) and Elephant/TaomHowdahStandingPoint.cs:102 (`MovingAgent.TeleportToPosition(GameEntity.GlobalPosition);`). Without it, remote creatures will visibly jitter or rubber-band.

findings.claim: Battle end-condition and side-depletion checks count only IsHuman agents. TAOM's humanoids pass, but a force composed entirely of mount-class creatures on one side would read as depleted/never-fielded.
findings.taom_impact: Low practical risk today (every TAOM troop rides its creature rather than being one), but TAOM must never ship a riderless-creature-only party template for coop. Same pattern in GameInterface.Services.MapEvents.Patches/CoopBattleDepletionPatch.cs:39.

findings.claim: TAOM's MissionLogics survive coop-launched battles: the coop launchers rebuild the vanilla behavior list but still use MissionState.OpenNew, and the engine calls every submodule's OnMissionBehaviorInitialize regardless of who built the list.
findings.taom_impact: No change needed to SubModule.OnMissionBehaviorInitialize — all 15+ TAOM behaviors (BehaviorTreeMissionLogic, AdvancedCombatBehavior, Warg/Spider/Elephant/Mumakil, MixedFormations, SmartCavalryAI, BannerBearerAssignmentMissionLogic) are added to coop field and siege battles. Coop's list also includes BannerBearerLogic and MountAgentLogic, which TAOM's banner-bearer logic depends on.

findings.claim: Coop's own mission behavior does NOT trip TAOM's known MissionLogic-cast regression: CoopMissionController derives from MissionBehavior but reports BehaviorType Other, so it is excluded from Mission.MissionLogics.
findings.evidence_quote: public abstract class CoopMissionController : MissionBehavior, IDisposable
findings.taom_impact: No action. TAOM's MissionDiagnosticBehavior 'BehaviorType=Logic + !MissionLogic null-cast offenders' scan will not flag Coop.

findings.claim: Weapon combat does NOT diverge despite TAOM's per-blow MBRandom draws: the blow is resolved once on the attacker's machine and replayed verbatim, so TaomCombatMechanicsModel's crush-through roll and TAOM's damage models are authoritative and never re-rolled by the receiver.
findings.taom_impact: TAOM's combat GameModel overrides need no determinism work. Coop registers no GameModel of its own (only NoHarmony scaffolding in Coop.Lib.NoHarmony), so TAOM's gamemodel-registry entries are untouched. Fidelity caveat: WeaponComponentDataSurrogate reconstructs the routed weapon with a null Item back-reference, affecting hit-sound/skill attribution only.

findings.claim: Hideout missions have no coop entry point. Coop patches CampaignMission.OpenBattleMission, OpenIndoorMission and OpenVillageMission, and launches sieges/tournaments through its own launchers, but there is no hideout hook anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence_quote: [HarmonyPatch(typeof(CampaignMission), "OpenBattleMission", new Type[] { typeof(MissionInitializerRecord) })]
findings.taom_impact: TAOM's hideout content (any lair/hideout battle with creatures) is unsynced — grep for OpenHideout across the whole decompiled tree returned NOT FOUND. TAOM should either treat hideouts as single-player-only in coop or accept that each peer plays its own instance.

findings.claim: Settlement/tavern/village walkabout missions block ALL damage involving a remote player puppet, in both directions.
findings.taom_impact: Any TAOM feature that inflicts damage inside a settlement scene (arena brawls, tavern fights, creature ambushes in town) is a no-op against other players in coop. TAOM should not build combat features that assume settlement missions replicate damage.

findings.claim: Coop hard-caps rendered agents at 2000 and clamps vanilla spawn counts to that budget; a mount costs 2 slots.
findings.evidence_quote: public int MaxRenderedAgents => 2000;
findings.taom_impact: TAOM's creature mounts (warg/spider/mumakil) are horse-component items so they correctly cost 2 slots via `itemObject.HasHorseComponent`. Large TAOM battles with heavy cavalry will hit the clamp earlier than in single-player; TAOM's TroopWeight party-size deflation interacts with, but does not conflict with, this cap.

findings.claim: The Monster constructor is Harmony-prefixed and returns false on clients, but the policy that permits it is state-gated and allows the original outside CampaignState/MissionState, so XML-time monster construction is safe.
findings.taom_impact: No action expected — ClientSyncPolicy.AllowOriginal() returns true unless the client state is CampaignState or MissionState, and module-data XML load precedes both. TAOM must nonetheless never construct a Monster at runtime during a live campaign/mission (it does not today — all monsters are XML).

findings.claim: Every locally spawned agent is captured and broadcast — replication is not limited to player agents. Any agent TAOM spawns through Mission.SpawnAgent during a coop battle is broadcast to all peers as a puppet.
findings.taom_impact: If TAOM ever spawns agents mid-battle (summons, howdah crew re-spawn, scripted reinforcements) each peer will spawn its own copy AND broadcast it, producing duplicates. Any TAOM mid-battle spawn must be gated to a single owner, or must set BattleSpawnGate.SuppressCapture (public static in GameInterface) around the call.

findings.claim: The elephant howdah machine has no replication path — coop replicates only siege machines/engines/ladders, not arbitrary UsableMachines.
findings.evidence_quote: builder.RegisterType<CoopBattleController>().AsSelf().InstancePerDependency();
findings.taom_impact: TaomHowdahMachine / TaomHowdahStandingPoint occupancy and the per-tick crew TeleportToPosition are purely local. The howdah is already DEFERRED-disabled in TAOM; do not re-enable it for coop without a replication story.

open_questions: Does the native engine fire Mission.MeleeHitCallback for a Controller=None puppet playing a replicated attack animation? If yes, vanilla weapon melee already double-applies in coop (owner routes its blow AND the observer computes one locally against its own agent), because BattleBlowInterceptPatch gates only on the VICTIM being a puppet and the attacker-side gates in the Missions assembly are never applied. Not determinable from managed source; needs a live two-peer test with a damage log.

Do all TAOM/LOTRLOME races define a `<race>_settlement` monster variant? GameInterface.Services.Locations/LocationCharacterFactory.cs:43 calls `FaceGen.GetMonsterWithSuffix(character.Race, "_settlement")` unguarded for every location character. The LOTRLOME snapshot shows _settlement variants for dwarf/uruk/orc/goblin/nazghul/troll/cave_troll/berserker/saruman — confirm no TAOM race added since lacks one.

Does BattleAgentSpawnData round-trip TAOM ItemModifiers on creature-mount harnesses? PuppetSpawner.ResolveMissionWeapon reconstructs MissionWeapon from an ItemObject id + ItemModifier surrogate, but SpawnEquipment goes through EquipmentSurrogate — worth a targeted check for TAOM's modified creature barding.

What happens to TAOM's MixedFormationsMissionBehavior formation reassignment under coop? Coop replicates only the FormationIndex captured at spawn (BattleAgentSpawnData.FormationIndex) and AgentFormationAssigner re-derives from `agent.Character.GetFormationClass()`; TAOM's post-spawn reassignment runs independently on each peer and may diverge.

Is there a version/module-set handshake at session join? Nothing in the read files enforces identical module lists, yet action replication (AgentActionData index round-trip) and object-id resolution (StringId registries) both silently corrupt if the peers' loaded data differs.
